compounding_issues: Every session was blocked before the model could act by an infra rate/session limit ("You've hit your session limit · resets 2:10am (Europe/Berlin)"); 0 tokens, 0 tool calls, exit_code 1 on all 5 sessions

Seed codebase mismatch: the committed seed (app.py) is a Flask/SQLite Todo API, wholly incongruent with the 'WebSocket notification server' story domain — a bad seed that would have compounded had any session run
Empty commits masked as progress: each session committed only the .instrument/session_N.jsonl marker, so the log shows 5 'story' commits with zero code changes, misleading downstream measurement

No-op output was misread as stability: analysis flags the untouched seed as 'stable — output matches baseline' / 'converged_back', so a total failure scored as a conservative, non-divergent trajectory
test_executed_success=false with zero tests ever run — instrumentation could not validate anything across the whole story
key_decisions: Intended architecture (from prompts only): WebSocket transport with per-client unique IDs, named channel subscriptions, Redis pub/sub message backbone, pluggable Transport interface, and per-client Redis rate-limit counters with persistent history
Chose the task ladder greenfield → feature_addition → integration → refactor → cross_cutting — a logically coherent plan that was never executed
Seeded the story with the wrong codebase (Flask Todo API) instead of a notification-service skeleton — the seed, not the agent, determined the only code ever present
No real engineering decisions were made: the agent produced zero code, so all 'choices' exist only in the session prompts
story_review.trajectory_description: The quality arc is flat at zero: the 5-session run consumed no tokens, cost $0.00, and changed nothing — app.py remained the 128-line Flask Todo seed from the initial commit. Session quality neither improved nor degraded because the model never executed; each session's sole artifact was a 3-line instrumentation JSONL recording the same rate-limit wall (resets 2:10am Europe/Berlin). The only meaningful change across commits was the incrementing session-number suffix on the .instrument files. Downstream metrics then inverted this total failure into a 'stable baseline' verdict, since no-op output trivially 'matches' the seed.
story_review.summary: A fully infrastructure-blocked run — every session was stopped by a rate limit before the model acted, so the 'progressive' 5-commit story is five empty commits over an incongruent Todo-API seed, producing zero code, zero tokens, and no measurable quality.
